ai.description: The Pakistani Agama reaches 12 cm in snout-vent length. It is grey-brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark dorsal blotches. Distinctive features include a flattened body and a spiny, whorled tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Laudakia pakistanica* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, enlarged, and spinose patch of scales on the sides of the neck, which is absent in other Indian *Laudakia*.
ai.habitat: *Laudakia pakistanica* inhabits rocky, arid slopes and boulder-strewn terrain in the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Pakistani Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently basks on rocky outcrops, retreating into deep crevices to escape predators or extreme temperatures.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laudakia pakistanica* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally from late spring through summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laudakia pakistanica* is endemic to northern Pakistan, primarily inhabiting the high-altitude rocky terrains of the Hindu Kush and Karakoram ranges in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
